title: Homography warp: a live DOM screen set into a drawing by four corners
intent: A live screen inside a picture
summary: A real HTML app (text, a button, a CSS loop) in a fixed box sized from its scene (at most 640 px, 86 % of the width, 62 % of the height, 16:10) is carried from its flat layout box onto the four corners of a drawn laptop screen: the corners are read off an SVG polygon through `getScreenCTM()`, so the `slice` crop and scale of the drawing are included, and re-read by a ResizeObserver; the scroll through a `280svh` sticky stage, smoothstepped over `.12–.78` of it, lerps each corner from flat to target, and the 2D homography from the rectangle to those points (eight unknowns, Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting) is written as one `matrix3d` with `transform-origin: 0 0`, `none` at the start; the browser hit-tests, selects and focuses through the same matrix; a glass quad above fades in with the landing, the box shadow and corner radius fade out; one scroll listener and one frame; the loop runs only while playing and on screen, behind the app's own Pause button; reduced motion and static drop the rail and sit placed and paused
variants: scrubbed from flat into the drawing (this, default)
always placed: the same solve on load and on resize only, for device mock-ups in a case study
a <video> or canvas in place of the app, warped into a photograph whose corners are given as fractions of the image
